title: Policy rejected by the API
scenario: "The governance pipeline failed: Azure refused our tag policy with UnsupportedPolicyRuleField. Until it is fixed, the platform guardrails initiative cannot be assigned and new resource groups go unchecked." — Cloud Governance lead
mission: Fix the require-rg-tags rule so Azure accepts it, ship it through a branch, and get the whole platform-guardrails initiative assigned.
objectives: Read an Azure Policy error and map it to the exact rule property
Test object keys with containsKey / notContainsKey and keep current() out of field accessors and field()
Understand why terraform validate and CI could not catch this error
Finish a partially applied layer safely

prerequisites.notes: Signed in with the lab account on the lab subscription.

cost: None — policy definitions and assignments are free.

steps.title: Locate the rule
steps.detail: The HCL only loads the file: find which JSON file under infra/policies/ holds the rule and the exact block named in the error.

steps.title: Write your hypothesis
steps.detail: Before editing: why does the engine reject a dynamic field? Which fixed path holds all the tags, and which operator asks whether an object has a key?

steps.title: Edit and commit
steps.detail: Change only the where clause of the value count. Keep the count over [parameters('tagNames')] and the greater: 0 comparison. Commit on your branch.

steps.title: Apply the layer
steps.detail: Re-run the plan: only the three missing resources (tags policy, initiative, assignment) should be created. Read the Plan line before typing y.

steps.title: Open the PR
steps.detail: Push the branch and open a PR. Required checks must be green before merging.

criteria.text: The rule uses no runtime function (such as current()) inside a field accessor or inside field()
criteria.how: Open infra/policies/require-rg-tags.rule.json and replace the where block (lines 24–27). The tag name must not go inside "field" (nor inside the field() function) — the Learn tab shows the allowed pattern.

criteria.text: The value count over tagNames tests the resource's tag keys against current('tagName')
criteria.how: Point "field" at the whole tags object ("tags") and ask with the notContainsKey operator whether it lacks [current('tagName')]. Save the file — the check runs by itself.

criteria.text: The fixed rule is committed on your branch (no uncommitted change)
criteria.how: In the terminal: git add infra/policies/require-rg-tags.rule.json, then git commit -m "fix(policy): ..." (on your fix/ branch, never on main).

criteria.text: Policy definition mfs-require-rg-tags exists in Azure with the fixed rule
criteria.how: In the terminal: ./scripts/azp.ps1 apply 20-governance — read the Plan line (expect 3 to add, 0 to destroy) and answer y.

criteria.text: Initiative mfs-platform-guardrails exists, references requireRgTags and is assigned to the subscription
criteria.how: Created by the same apply 20-governance. If it is still red after the apply, press Check — Azure can take a minute to show it.

expectedResult: 20-governance fully applied (9/9). The initiative shows in Azure Policy → Assignments, and compliance starts evaluating resource groups in Audit mode.

concepts.title: What an Azure Policy is
concepts.body:
A policy is a rule that Azure evaluates against every resource in a scope (a subscription, for example). Every rule has the same shape: IF a condition is true THEN apply an effect such as `Audit` (just report) or `Deny` (block the request).

Several policies can be grouped into an *initiative* (policy set) and assigned once. That is what `mfs-platform-guardrails` is.

concepts.title: Conditions: field vs value — and where current() may appear
concepts.body:
A condition compares a left side with an operator such as `equals`, `exists`, `containsKey` or `notContainsKey`.

`field` is a FIXED path to a property of the resource (`location`, `name`, `tags`, `tags['Owner']`). It may use `parameters()`, but not runtime functions such as `current()`.

`value` is any ARM expression in square brackets; inside it you can call `field('path')` — but the argument of `field()` must not contain runtime functions either.

Where `current()` IS allowed: on the value side of an operator (`"notContainsKey": "[current('tagName')]"`) and in `value` expressions outside `field()`.

concepts.title: Loops: the value count
concepts.body:
A `count` with a `value` walks a list (here: the list of mandatory tag names). For every item, it evaluates the `where` condition; the item is available as `current('tagName')`. The outer comparison (`greater: 0`) asks: "is there at least one item for which `where` is true?".

So `where` must answer: "is THIS tag missing on the resource group?".

concepts.title: Testing keys of an object
concepts.body: The tags of a resource are one object (`{"Owner": "x", "Environment": "lab"}`) at the fixed path `tags`. `containsKey` / `notContainsKey` ask whether that object has a given key — and the key can come from an expression on the value side, such as the current item of a loop.

glossary.def: A set of policies assigned together, with shared parameters (policy set definition).
`Audit` reports non-compliance; `Deny` blocks the request; `Disabled` turns the rule off.
A formula in square brackets, e.g. `[concat('a', 'b')]`, evaluated by Azure Resource Manager.
API error: the rule uses something the policy engine does not allow in that position.

recovery: A failed apply is safe to repeat: Terraform already stored the resources it created, so the next apply creates only what is missing. If the plan wants to destroy anything, stop and investigate.
dont: Do not create the policy in the portal
Do not switch the effect to Deny in this session
hints: The error says field accessors and the field() function cannot contain runtime functions such as current(). Where else in a condition can current() appear?
current() is allowed on the VALUE side of an operator. The tags of a resource are one object at the fixed path "tags" — which operator checks whether an object has a given key?
Docs: "Azure Policy definition structure — policy rule", sections "Conditions" (containsKey / notContainsKey) and "Value count". Your where clause needs "field": "tags" and one key operator.

interview.question: A policy passed terraform validate and CI but Azure rejected it on apply. How do you prevent that class of failure?
followUps: What is the difference between field and value conditions?

debrief: The where clause became { "field": "tags", "notContainsKey": "[current('tagName')]" }. The engine forbids runtime functions (current(), field(), resourceGroup()…) inside a field accessor AND inside the field() function — both the original rule and the first "fix" with field(concat(…current…)) were rejected at PUT time. Keeping the path fixed ("tags") and moving current() to the operator's value side is allowed. Lesson: Terraform and JSON validation only check syntax; the Azure Resource Manager validates policy semantics on PUT. Mitigations: deploy policies to a sandbox scope first, keep rules small, and test them with known compliant / non-compliant resources.

validation.notes: Local, git and Azure failing paths proven on the live environment; the passing path is proven with a fake Azure CLI in tests. A real pass needs your fix + apply.
